chunks: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari from Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Lu'lu'i from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When you fast for the sighting of the crescent and break your fast for its sighting, you have completed the month, even if you did not fast except for twenty-nine days. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The month is like this, like this, and like this,
and he gestured with his hand ten, ten, and ten, and like this, like this, and like this:
ai.seo_question: How is the completion of the fasting month determined if only twenty-nine days are fasted?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the lunar calendar mechanics by affirming that the month of Ramadan is completed upon the sighting of the Shawwal crescent, even if only twenty-nine days of fasting were observed. It cites the Prophet’s gesture—indicating ten, ten, and nine—to illustrate the variable nature of the lunar cycle (29 or 30 days), a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding the determination of Eid al-Fitr. This ruling underscores the reliance on actual observation (*ru'yah*) over fixed arithmetic calculations in traditional Shia legal theory.
